name: Subset Teaching Dimension of Cube–Half-interval Product
proof: For $m\ge1,n\ge2$, the two factors have STD $m$ and one, respectively, by the full-cube and half-interval calculations. Proposition \ref{prop:subset-teaching-product} proves that STD is additive for nonempty finite classes on disjoint domains: at every iteration, the full family of minimum samples for a product target consists exactly of unions of factor minimizers, because their containment sets factor as a Cartesian product. Applying that identity gives $m+1$. The nonempty initial-segment convention, including its constant first coordinate, is the one used in the half-interval value proof.
